title: Shared definitions
description: Definitions used by more than one protocol document. SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0. Identifiers are URNs on purpose: nothing in a schema is ever fetched (S1).

libraryId.description: Namespace identifier of a library. Lower case; reverse-DNS form (org.example.lib) for verified namespaces, a short name (qet-official) for the project's own. Resolution is namespace-authoritative (S5): no source answers for a namespace it does not own.

uuid.description: Element UUID as written in the .elmt file: lower-case hex, with or without braces. Stable across renames and moves.

version.description: Element version, major.minor.patch, assigned by the publisher. Anything touching a port is major (part D §5).

hash.description: Content hash: 'sha256:' followed by 64 lower-case hex digits.

relayUri.description: Opaque relay endpoint at the publishing host, which forwards to the contributor it has verified (part D §3.5). Never an e-mail address or any other direct address of a person; hence https only. A persistent pseudonymous identifier for a publisher, never for a reader (S8).

usage.description: Usage declaration (part D §4, §18.3). Mandatory at library level, inside the signed feed; optional per element, where it overrides the library's. There is deliberately no default anywhere: a feed without a library-level block is rejected, never defaulted (annex §10.1.1).

train-ai.description: IETF AIPREF: may the content be used to train AI models.

ai-use.description: IETF AIPREF: may the content be used as input to AI systems at use time.

search.description: IETF AIPREF: may the content be used to build a search index.

policy.description: Human-readable policy page. Displayed as text and never dereferenced by a client (S1).

representation.description: Which kind of view an element is (part D §13.3). An OPEN vocabulary: a registered core, plus namespaced extensions of the form <reverse-dns>:<name>. A schema that closed this set would make the vocabulary closed in practice, so unregistered namespaced values must validate.

articleId.description: Identifies an article (a physical product), never an element. At least one of the identifiers must be present.

lifecycle.description: Coarse ARTICLE lifecycle (part D §5, 'Two lifecycles'). Sourced from the library's metadata file, never from the .elmt, so that a discontinuation cannot change a drawing's hash. Authoritative only from the manufacturer's own namespace. Absent means unknown, never active.

successor.description: Successor ARTICLE, not an element UUID. Not a drop-in replacement.

extensions.description: Namespaced extensions, keyed by a domain name (x-example.org or example.org). Clients must ignore unknown extensions; the core never depends on them.
